 KTAL Shreveport Follow Dry weather continues with cold air coming
 Todd Warren Mon, November 9, 2026 at 9:01 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. SHREVEPORT, LA (KTAL/KMSS) - The dry weather pattern that has returned to the ArkLaTex will likely continue through the rest of this week.  Temperatures will stay above normal until a surge of cold air invades the area this weekend. 
 Tomorrow's Forecast
 Pleasant temperatures continue: Temperatures will likely remain above normal for the next several days. Tuesday will begin with lows in the low to middle 50s. Daytime highs on Tuesday will warm into the middle 70s. We will likely be a little warmer on Wednesday. 
 Futurecast outlook for the next 48 hours
 Expect the return of more sunshine:   We have seen quite a few clouds over much of the ArkLaTex on Monday.  They will likely stick around on Monday night. Rain will remain unlikely, even though Futurecast shows some showers over the northern part of the area. Other models keep us dry. Clouds will decrease on Tuesday, and we will see a partly cloudy sky on Wednesday.
 Long-range rain:  Once again today, the seven-day rainfall outlook from the Weather Prediction Center shows very little rain for the ArkLaTex from now through next Monday.  There are still some signs that the chance of rain will begin to return by the middle of next week. 
 10-day rainfall potential outlook from the Blend of Models
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Coldest air of the season? A surge of cold air from Canada will spread over the ArkLaTex this weekend.  Temperatures ahead of its arrival will stay above normal, with lows in the 50s and highs in the 50s.  This weekend, daytime highs will fall into the mid to upper 60s.  Overnight lows will fall into the 30s and lower 40s. The chill won't be here long.  Lows will return to the 50s and highs to the low to middle 70s by the middle of next week. 
 10-Day Forecast for Shreveport
 Tune in to my live show, Weather Worries, at 8:30 pm on the KTAL Now app on your smart TV.  You can also see it here.   Tonight is 'Grain of Salt' night.  I will share the latest outlook on potential temperatures and rainfall that we will experience during the next six weeks. That's live tonight at 8:30 pm.  Talk to you then!
